data.name: Denyse
data.long_meaning: From the Greek name 'Dionysia', derived from 'Dionysos', meaning 'God of Wine' or 'God of the Dead'. In Christianity, the name Denyse is associated with the virtue of denying oneself for the sake of God and others. This name is a reminder of the spiritual gift of selflessness.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of humility and self-denial, embodying the Christian virtue of putting others before oneself.
data.numerology_meaning: In numerology, Denyse is associated with the number 1, representing new beginnings, independence, and leadership. Individuals with this name may have a strong desire to be their own person, and they are natural born leaders.

in_hebrew.name: דניס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם דניס מקורו בשם היווני דניסוס, שפירושו אל היין והפריון. במסורת הנוצרית, השם דניס משויך לקדוש דניס, אב המנזר של כנסיית סן דני בפריס. השם דניס פירושו 'קדוש', 'מוקדש לאל', ומשקף את חשיבות הקדושה והמסירות לאלוהים במסורת הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Δηνύση
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Δηνύση προέρχεται από το γαλλικό Denyse, που είναι η θηλυκή μορφή του ονόματος Denis. Το όνομα Denis προέρχεται από το λατινικό Dionysius, που σημαίνει 'ακολουθός του Διόνυσος'. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Δηνύση συνδέεται με τον Άγιο Διονύσιο, έναν από τους πρώτους χριστιανούς ιεράρχες.

in_latin.name: Denyse
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Denyse originem trahit a gallico Denyse, quod est forma feminina nominis Denis. Nomen Denis derivatur a latino Dionysius, quod significat 'sectator Dionysi'. In traditione ecclesiastica, nomen Denyse refertur ad Sanctum Dionysium, unum ex primis hierarchis christianis.

in_english.name: Denyse
in_english.long_meaning: The name Denyse is derived from the Greek name Dionysius, which means 'follower of Dionysus'. In Christian tradition, Denyse is associated with Saint Denis, a 3rd-century martyr and saint. The name Denyse symbolizes devotion to God, holiness, and spiritual dedication. It reflects the values of faith, piety, and commitment to one's beliefs.

saint_reference.note: Saint Denis was a 3rd-century martyr and saint, often associated with France.

data.cultural_impact: Denyse derives from the Greek name 'Dionysia', which was the name of a ancient Greek goddess of wine, fertility, and theater. In Christianity, the name Denyse lost its connection with its ancient roots and took on new meaning as a name associated with selflessness and denial.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Denyse is a reminder of the spiritual gift of selflessness. In the Bible, Jesus encourages us to love our neighbors as ourselves (Matthew 22:39), which requires denying our own desires and wants in order to serve and care for others. The name Denyse invites us to emulate the selflessness of Christ, who humbled himself and became obedient even unto death (Philippians 2:8). Denying oneself for the sake of God and others is a powerful spiritual discipline that deepens our relationship with God and brings lasting joy and fulfillment.

historical_references.reference: Denyse of Poitiers, a Christian martyr who was beheaded in 481 AD for refusing to renounce her faith.
historical_references.context: Denyse was a Christian martyr who was beheaded in Poitiers, France, for her refusal to renounce her faith during the Roman Empire.

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names.
